name: Clawproof Production Gate

questions.01a: Is every tool permission declared in a version-controlled manifest and enforced at the agent runtime, not just at the downstream API?
questions.01b: Is there a recurring audit (weekly or monthly) that compares granted permissions against actual usage, and revokes unused ones?
questions.02a: Does every agent interaction produce a structured log entry that captures the input, retrieved context, tool calls with parameters, tool results, and final output?
questions.02b: Are logs tamper-evident (append-only, signed, or in an audit-grade store) and retained long enough to support regulatory or incident investigations?
questions.03a: Do automated prompt-injection tests verify that untrusted content cannot override trusted instructions or expand tool permissions?
questions.03b: Are outbound tool calls constrained so the agent cannot send data to arbitrary destinations (no open URL fetch, no arbitrary email recipients, no free-form webhooks)?
questions.04a: For every agent capability, is there a declared threshold (financial, legal, reputational, confidence-based) above which the agent must pause for human approval?
questions.04b: Is the escalation path itself tested — does a real human actually receive, review, and either approve or deny the pause within the declared SLA?
questions.05a: Is there a single documented action (one button, one CLI command, one feature flag) that stops the agent from taking any new action within 30 seconds?
questions.05b: For each destructive or public-facing capability, is there a reversible path — dry-run mode, staging replay, compensating transaction — that can undo recent agent actions?
questions.06a: Are all secrets injected via a secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, environment of the orchestrator) rather than hardcoded in prompts, configs, or repo files?
questions.06b: Is there automated scanning — at commit time and at log-write time — that prevents secrets from leaking into repos, logs, telemetry, or agent outputs?
questions.07a: Is there a versioned evaluation suite with representative inputs, expected behaviors, and automated grading that runs on every model or prompt change?
questions.07b: Do production releases require the eval suite to pass with no regressions against the previous version, not just absolute score thresholds?
questions.08a: Does the retrieval layer enforce access-control at query time (row-level security, per-user corpora, ACL filters) — not just at the UI layer of the source system?
questions.08b: Is the RAG corpus audited for data classes (PII, PHI, trade secrets, legal-privileged, retention-limited) with a declared policy for each, including what may not be indexed at all?
questions.09a: Is there a hard spending cap, enforced at the orchestration layer, that halts the agent when daily/hourly cost crosses a declared threshold?
questions.09b: Are per-agent and per-user rate limits enforced independently of the LLM provider's own limits, with alerts firing before limits are hit?
questions.10a: When multiple agents access shared resources, is there a coordination layer (locks, queues, transactional commits, conflict-resolution rules) that prevents race conditions and inconsistent writes?
questions.10b: Are messages between agents cryptographically or structurally distinguishable from user or external inputs, so no agent treats peer output as a user instruction?

decision_rules.review: Any partial, no, unknown, omitted answer, or yes answer without an evidence reference.
decision_rules.pass: Every question answered yes and every answer has at least one evidence reference.
decision_rules.precedence: BLOCK takes precedence over REVIEW, which takes precedence over PASS.

evaluation_rules.answers: Use only the lowercase values yes, partial, no, and unknown.
evaluation_rules.unexpected_question_ids: Reject question ids that are not in question_ids.
evaluation_rules.evidence_references: Require an array of non-empty strings and trim surrounding whitespace.
evaluation_rules.omitted_answers: Normalize omitted answers to unknown and require REVIEW.

disclaimer: This gate evaluates declared answers and evidence references. It does not inspect or certify a production environment.
